name: PY32F002AF15P6TR
title: PY32F002A series 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ microcontroller, 24 MHz, 20 KB flash, 3 KB SRAM
summary: The PY32F002A family is a small Cortex-M0+ microcontroller running at up to 24 MHz from a single 1.7 V to 5.5 V supply, with 20 KB of flash and 3 KB of SRAM. It carries a 12-bit ADC with up to nine external inputs, two comparators, an advanced and a general-purpose 16-bit timer, a low-power timer, a watchdog, and one each of SPI, I2C and USART. Seven package variants run from 8 to 20 pins; the PY32F002AF15P is the TSSOP20 part with 18 I/O, and PY32F002AF15P6TR is that part rated -40 to 85 °C on tape and reel.
key_figures: 1.5 mA typ, HSI 24 MHz, peripherals on

notes: Every variant has one 16-bit advanced timer, one 16-bit general-purpose timer, one low-power timer, SysTick, a watchdog, one SPI, one I2C and one USART, runs to 24 MHz and from 1.7 V to 5.5 V.
An orderable code adds the temperature digit and packing to the base number: PY32F002AF15P6TR is the TSSOP20 part, temperature code 6 (-40 to +85 °C), tape and reel.

operation.text: Voltages are measured against VSS. Minimum and maximum limits are screened in volume production at 25 °C and at the top of the ambient range, and hold over the worst combination of temperature, supply and clock; limits footnoted as from characterization, simulation or design are not production tested and are set at the sample mean plus or minus three standard deviations. Typical figures are at 25 °C and VCC = 3.3 V and are untested guidance.

A Cortex-M0+ core with a two-stage pipeline and single-cycle multiplier runs at up to 24 MHz, with its NVIC closely coupled. SRAM (3 KB) takes byte, half-word and word access. Flash holds a 20 KB main area for code and data plus a 2.7 KB information area with the option bytes, the unique ID and the system memory. Read protection (RDP) blocks outside access, write protection (WRP) works in 4 KB units, and the option bytes have their own unlock sequence.

The BOOT0 pin and the nBOOT1 option bit choose where the core starts: BOOT0 low starts from main flash; BOOT0 high starts from system memory when nBOOT1 is 1 and from SRAM when nBOOT1 is 0. The system memory carries a boot loader that programs flash over the USART.

After start-up the system runs from HSI at 8 MHz; software can then change the source and frequency. Sources: HSI RC at 8 or 24 MHz, LSI RC at 32.768 kHz, and an HSE crystal oscillator of 4 to 24 MHz. A clock security system watches HSE; if HSE fails, hardware moves the system clock to HSI and raises an NMI. AHB is divided from SYSCLK by 1 to 512 and APB from AHB by 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16, both to at most 24 MHz; timers see PCLK times 1 when the APB prescaler is 1 and times 2 otherwise. The MCO output can carry SYSCLK, HSE, HSI or LSI through a divider of 1 to 128. LSI clocks the IWDG; LPTIM can run from PCLK or LSI.

With HSEBYP set in RCC_CR the oscillator's start-up circuit is off and an external clock of up to 24 MHz drives OSC_IN; the pin otherwise used by the oscillator is then an ordinary GPIO. The crystal or ceramic resonator runs from 4 to 32 MHz; output distortion and start-up settling time are smallest with the crystal and its load capacitors placed right at the pins.

One supply, VCC at 1.7 V to 5.5 V, feeds everything: the analog domain VCCA and the I/O domain VCCIO come from the VCC pad. An internal main regulator (MR) gives the 1.2 V core supply VDD for the logic and SRAM in run mode. In stop mode software keeps MR or switches to the low-power regulator (LPR), whose output is 1.2 V or 1.0 V.

The POR/PDR block stays active in every mode and holds the chip in reset below its thresholds (about 1.6 V rising, 1.55 V falling). The brown-out reset (BOR) is turned on or off only through the option bytes; when on, its rising threshold is one of eight levels from 1.8 V to 3.2 V typ and its falling threshold one of eight from 1.7 V to 3.1 V typ, each set on its own. After the supply crosses the threshold the reset is held for tRSTTEMPO (4.0 ms typ).

Sleep stops the CPU clock while chosen peripherals (NVIC, SysTick and others) keep running. Stop keeps SRAM and register contents, turns off HSI and HSE and halts most VDD-domain clocks; a GPIO event, a comparator output or LPTIM wakes it, and the IWDG ends it by reset. Wake-up takes 1.65 µs typ from sleep and 3.5 µs to 6 µs typ from stop.
A power reset comes from POR/PDR or BOR. A system reset comes from the NRST pin, the independent watchdog, a SYSRESETREQ software request, an option-byte load, or a power reset.

Each port bit is set by software as push-pull or open-drain output, floating, pull-up, pull-down or analog input, or an alternate function, and its configuration can be locked. Outputs drive 8 mA. Pins are floating inputs during and after reset, except PA13 (SWDIO, pull-up), PA14 (SWCLK, pull-down) and PF4-BOOT0 (input, pull-down). An option byte chooses whether PF2 is a GPIO or the NRST input.

The NVIC takes one NMI and 32 maskable interrupts plus 10 Cortex-M0+ exceptions, with 4 priority levels, nesting and tail-chaining. EXTI lines cover up to 16 GPIOs (any port bit routed to lines 0 to 15), the two comparator outputs and the LPTIM wake-up; GPIO and comparator lines trigger on rising, falling or both edges, each line can be masked, it catches pulses narrower than one internal clock cycle, and the latched source can be read after waking from stop.

A 12-bit SAR ADC converts up to 11 channels, 9 external and 2 internal, over 0 to VCC. Each channel runs single, continuous, scan or discontinuous conversion, with results left- or right-aligned in 16-bit registers. An analog watchdog flags inputs above or below set limits, and interrupts can be raised at the end of sampling, of a conversion or of a sequence. A conversion takes 12 ADC clocks.

Two comparators take their inputs from I/O pins, VCC, the temperature sensor, or VREFINT and its 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 fractions. Hysteresis and the speed/power trade-off are programmable. The output can go to a pin or to a timer, as an OCREF_CLR event for cycle-by-cycle current control or as a break input for fast PWM shutdown. Each comparator can interrupt and, through EXTI, wake the chip from sleep or stop.

TIM1 is a 16-bit advanced timer with a 16-bit prescaler, up, down and center-aligned counting, 4 channels for input capture, output compare, edge- or center-aligned PWM and one-pulse output, 3 complementary outputs with dead-time insertion, 0 to 100 % modulation, and chaining with other timers. TIM16 is a 16-bit general-purpose timer with a 16-bit prescaler. The low-power timer LPTIM counts up over 16 bits behind a 3-bit prescaler, in single-count mode only, and can wake the chip from stop. All three can freeze in debug mode.

The independent watchdog runs from LSI, so it keeps counting if the main clock fails, and resets the system when it times out; an option byte can start it in hardware mode, and it can freeze in debug. Its timeout spans 0.122 ms to 31981.568 ms with the LSI clock. SysTick is a 24-bit auto-reload down counter with a maskable interrupt at zero, meant for an RTOS tick or general timing.

One I2C interface works as master or slave, multi-master capable, in standard mode (100 kHz) and fast mode (400 kHz), with 7-bit addressing, general call, optional clock stretching, software reset, and an analog noise filter on SDA and SCL. As master it generates the clock and the start and stop conditions; as slave it detects its programmed address and the stop bit. Status flags cover direction, byte done and busy; error flags cover arbitration loss, missing ACK, start/stop error and over/underrun.

USART1 does full-duplex asynchronous NRZ transfers with a fractional baud-rate generator up to 4.5 Mbit/s, automatic baud-rate detection, 8- or 9-bit data, 1 or 2 stop bits, 16x or 8x oversampling, parity generation and check, synchronous mode with a clock output, single-wire half-duplex, hardware flow control (RTS/CTS), and multiprocessor mute mode left by idle-line or address-mark detection.

One SPI runs as master or slave in full duplex, half duplex on a bidirectional line, or simplex, with 8- or 16-bit frames, multi-master support, hardware or software NSS, programmable clock polarity and phase, and MSB- or LSB-first order. The master baud rate has 8 prescaler settings up to fPCLK/4, and slave mode also runs up to fPCLK/4. It uses the Motorola frame format, with interrupt flags for transmit, receive, mode fault and overrun.
A two-wire Arm SWD port on PA13 (SWDIO) and PA14 (SWCLK) connects a debugger.

The temperature sensor gives 0.76 V typ at 30 °C with a 2.5 mV/°C average slope and needs at least 9 µs of ADC sampling time. The internal reference VREFINT is 1.2 V typ (1.17 V to 1.23 V) and draws 12 µA typ from VCC.
